basis: Central saccade-initiation disorder; ataxia 80-99% and cerebellar abnormalities 30-79%. Intrinsic eye damage is not established; strabismus is only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: impaired central initiation of saccades defines the disease; ataxia occurs in 80-99% and cerebellar malformations in 30-79%.
decisions.ocular: none: impaired gaze reflects central motor control rather than intrinsic eye disease; strabismus and nystagmus occur in only 5-29%.

basis: Malignancy originates in laryngeal cartilage, part of the upper airway; its cartilaginous histology does not establish locomotor-system involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the site of origin is the laryngeal airway framework, not bone, joints or connective tissue of the locomotor system.

basis: Glycerol metabolism defect; developmental delay 12/14 (~86%) and intellectual disability 2/4 support neurologic involvement. Complex deletions enrich these data; pancreatitis 1/4 excluded.

decisions.neurologic: involved: supplied HPO reports developmental delay in 12/14 (~86%) and intellectual disability in 2/4; these exceed 30%, despite enrichment for complex deletions.

basis: Marrow disease and the diagnostic mucocutaneous triad include oral leukoplakia (4/12). Pulmonary fibrosis 3/12 (25%) and cirrhosis 2/12 (17%) are below threshold.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral leukoplakia is part of the defining dyskeratosis congenita triad and occurs in 4/12 (~33%); oral mucosa belongs to gastrointestinal.

basis: Brain and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; calvarial abnormalities 80-99%. Oral clefts and strabismus each 30-79%; nonspecific immune physiology does not establish immune damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: defining skeletal malformations include abnormal digits and caudal deficiency; calvarial abnormalities and micrognathia occur in 80-99%.

basis: Symphalangism is congenital fusion of digital joints. The supplied record establishes no dental or oral abnormality or frequency supporting another axis.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental/oral malformations are asserted by one label, but the supplied disease record establishes neither a defining oral lesion nor its frequency.

basis: Purine metabolic disorder; renal insufficiency 30-79%. Neurologic/hearing damage belongs to severe disease (~25%); HPO overrepresents this subtype. Gout and stones are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurodevelopmental damage characterizes the severe form (~25% overall); the predominant mild form lacks it. HPO ataxia frequencies reflect severe-case enrichment.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss belongs to the severe form (~25% overall); the HPO 80-99% annotation is not representative across the mild-predominant umbrella.

basis: Lysosomal storage and skeletal dysplasia define this umbrella. Neurologic damage varies by constituent disease; a representative frequency of at least 30% is not established.

decisions.neurologic: none: neuronopathic subtypes occur within this group, but their presence alone does not establish neurologic damage in at least 30% across the entire umbrella.

basis: Hantaviral infection with defining renal and hemorrhagic blood dysfunction; direct endothelial barrier failure causes capillary leak in 80-99%. Pulmonary disease is only 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: capillary leak in 80-99% reflects direct endothelial barrier dysfunction with circulatory impairment, rather than an isolated transient skin sign.

basis: Axonal neuropathy with defining optic atrophy and hearing loss; muscle wasting, skeletal deformities and contractures are typical (>30%). Respiratory impairment is variable.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is an explicit defining feature of this specific neuropathy syndrome; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss is an explicit defining feature of this specific syndrome, rather than an incidental complication.
